items.title: Listen to Erika de Casier’s New Song “Whispers”
items.summary:
Erika de Casier has released "Whispers," a standalone single that marks the Danish singer's first new music in roughly a year and a half. The track was co-produced by Eurohead, who has worked with Bladee and Yung Lean, and arrives with a video directed by Igor Pjörrt.

In the clip, de Casier and Atusa Zamani run along the scalloped beaches of an oceanside property before waking up at night inside a car. Pitchfork noted the single is not attached to an announced album, leaving it as a one-off for now.

The song follows Lifetime, which de Casier surprise-released in May of last year. She teased that record by putting a small run of white-label cassettes on Bandcamp, which sold out immediately, before making the album available online.

De Casier toured briefly behind Lifetime that fall and opened shows for Lorde and Robyn on select dates. "Whispers" is her first release since.

items.title: Don Toliver Announces Sixth Album ‘Nitrous,’ Due Next Month
items.summary:
Don Toliver has announced Nitrous, his sixth album, for release on December 4 through Cactus Jack, Donnway Co. and Atlantic Records. The Houston rapper recorded, produced and engineered the project entirely by himself, and announced it on social media with a clip showing him at work in a futuristic studio setup.

The album includes "Party With the Boys," which arrived last Friday alongside a video directed by Tyler Ross featuring Bam Margera. Toliver will follow the release with his first appearance on Saturday Night Live on December 5.

The announcement lands a day after Toliver picked up five Grammy nominations, as Variety reported. He is up for best new artist, best rap album for Octane, best rap performance for "Body," and both best rap song and best melodic rap performance for "E85."

Octane, released this past January, debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard 200. "E85" reached No. 3 on Billboard's Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs chart and No. 15 on the Hot 100.

Toliver spent most of the year touring behind the record. The Octane World Tour ran arena dates from May through July, then resumed in August as the Nitrous: New World Tour, a leg that wraps at London's O2 Arena at the end of November.

items.title: Newsmax Sues to Block Fox-Roku Deal
items.summary:
Newsmax has sued to unwind Fox Corp.'s $22 billion acquisition of Roku, arguing in a complaint filed Wednesday in California federal court that the deal hands Fox an effective monopoly in free ad-supported streaming. The conservative cable news channel, which relies on The Roku Channel to distribute its programming, also takes aim at the Justice Department's decision to clear the merger with minimal concessions.

Citing Nielsen data, the lawsuit says The Roku Channel accounts for roughly 42 percent of viewing time on free ad-supported services and Fox's Tubi for more than 28 percent, putting the combined company above 70 percent. That share, Newsmax argues, is presumptively anticompetitive. "DOJ virtually never clears a transaction combining the two leading competitors in a concentrated market," the complaint states, adding that regulators "allowed this merger to an effective monopoly to close unchallenged."

Fox closed the deal earlier this month, ahead of the 2027 target its executives had identified, and the Justice Department said hours after the announcement that it would not sue, concluding the transaction was "not likely to result in harm to competition." Under its arrangement with regulators, Fox agreed to keep carrying non-Fox movies and shows for at least three years, not to bury rival services in search results or home-screen placement, make audience data available to third parties and maintain information-sharing safeguards until at least 2029.

According to The Hollywood Reporter, Newsmax approached Fox because those commitments carried no enforcement mechanism and asked the company to sign an agreement making them binding. Fox declined. "Fox's failure to stand by the commitments in that press release underscores the need for judicial intervention," wrote David Schwarz, a lawyer for Newsmax, in the filing.

The complaint argues the merger gives Fox both content and distribution leverage: the company now owns Tubi and The Roku Channel, the premium service Fox One, and the operating system that powers Roku devices and is built into televisions, through which millions of households reach apps from Netflix, YouTube and Disney+. Newsmax says that combination lets Fox favor its own properties in search and recommendations while pushing competitors down.

A Fox spokesperson called the suit "wholly without merit," saying it "comes after a rigorous review process by regulatory agencies" and that the company "commenced actively integrating this approved transaction for the benefit of consumers, partners and other stakeholders." The deal had been more than a year in the making but closed in five months.
